title: Diameter, two tangents, and a parallel line
statement: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. From external P, PB and PC are tangents at B and C. Prove AC∥OP.
local_hints: Two tangents from P create two right angles and a symmetric kite.

title: Median meets the circumcircle again
statement: In △ABC, AB=9, BC=8, AC=7. M is the midpoint of BC. Line AM meets the circumcircle again at D. Find MD.
local_hints: M is both a midpoint and an interior chord-intersection point.

title: Four circles tangent to one line
statement: C1 and C2 each have radius 360 and are tangent to each other and the same line. C3 is tangent to C1,C2 and the line; C4 is tangent to C1,C3 and the line. Find the radius of C4.
local_hints: Flatten the picture: use the horizontal separation of circle centres above the common tangent.
Recall GEO-CIRCLEPACK-01 · Flatten tangent circles onto one baseline.
For two radii r,s on the same tangent line, use d=2√(rs). Find the middle radius first, then write one-dimensional centre gaps for C4.

title: Semicircle, midpoint of an arc, and two secants
statement: AB is the diameter of a semicircle. C lies on it, D is the midpoint of minor arc BC, and AD meets BC at E. Given CE=3 and BD=2√5, find AB.
local_hints: The midpoint of arc BC gives equal chords and makes AD an angle bisector.
Mark BD=DC and use AD as the angle bisector at A; translate that into a side ratio before bringing in the right-triangle data.

title: Square with two vertices on a circle and two on a tangent
statement: A square has two vertices on a circle of radius r and its other two vertices on a tangent to the circle. Find the side length.
local_hints: The square-circle-tangent configuration is symmetric about the radius perpendicular to the tangent.
Recall GEO-COORD-01 · Place coordinates to remove constraints.

title: Cyclic trapezium with circumcentre on a side
statement: A cyclic trapezium has its circumcentre on one parallel side. The parallel sides are in ratio 1:4. Find (sum of the two oblique sides)/(longer parallel side).
local_hints: A cyclic trapezium is isosceles, and a chord through the centre is a diameter.
Recall GEO-CIRCLE-01 · Track the chord or arc.

title: Maximum area with a fixed unit chord
statement: A circle has radius 1 and a fixed chord of length 1. What is the greatest area of an inscribed triangle using this chord as base?
local_hints: The chord is a fixed base, so only the perpendicular height controls the area.
Recall GEO-OPT-01 · Optimize the variable inside the target formula.

title: Incenter height in an isosceles triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC, AB=AC=15 and BC=10. The incircle has centre O, and P is the midpoint of BC. Find OP.
local_hints: In an isosceles triangle the incenter lies on the altitude through the base midpoint.
Recall GEO-CENTER-01 · Identify triangle centres from their defining lines.

title: Two common tangents
statement: Two circles touch at C. AB and CD are common tangents, with D on segment AB. If CD=4 cm, find AB.
local_hints: From D, each circle supplies a pair of equal tangent lengths.

title: Two internally tangent circles
statement: Two circles of radii 10 and 8 are internally tangent at A. The line of centres continues from A to the opposite point D of the larger circle. P is on the larger circle; secant PA meets the smaller circle again at B, and PM is tangent to the smaller circle. Given PM=2√5, find x=∠PAD.
local_hints: Internal tangency at A gives a homothety centred at A along ray AP.
Use the radius ratio to relate AB and AP first; then apply tangent-secant power from P before using the diameter right angle.

title: Four tangent circles — repeated revision problem
statement: C1 and C2 each have radius 360 and are tangent to each other and a common line. C3 is tangent to C1,C2 and the line; C4 is tangent to C1,C3 and the line. Find the radius of C4.
local_hints: This is the same common-baseline circle mechanism as Q21; retrieve it rather than start a new angle chase.
Recall GEO-CIRCLEPACK-01 · Flatten tangent circles onto one baseline.

title: Ptolemy identity in a square
statement: Square ABCD is inscribed in a circle and P lies on arc BC. Prove (PA+PC)/(PB+PD)=PD/PA.
local_hints: A square on one circle makes Ptolemy collapse because many chords are equal.
Recall GEO-PTOLEMY-01 · Turn a cyclic quadrilateral into one length equation.
Write Ptolemy for two cyclic quadrilaterals containing P and three square vertices; normalize the square side before eliminating repeated terms.

title: Ptolemy identity in a regular pentagon
statement: Regular pentagon ABCDE is inscribed in a circle and P lies on arc BC. Prove PA+PD=PB+PC+PE.
local_hints: A regular pentagon has only two polygon chord lengths: side and diagonal.
Recall GEO-PTOLEMY-01 · Turn a cyclic quadrilateral into one length equation.
Write two Ptolemy equations containing P; use one symbol for every pentagon diagonal and eliminate it.
